# Chapter Nine: The Messenger

> *"Behold, I will send my messenger and he will offer my words of honor and faith to the masses, for he will be my conduit in midworld."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

Nero surveyed the tree line, sitting by the side of the road resting his aching legs from the long journey. Buttoning up the heavy fur lined coat, the cold wind of winter biting into his exposed skin, looking to his traveling partners he could see the discomfort apparent on their faces as they do bundled up.

“That’s the tenth story we have heard in so many days” Nero exclaimed, his face looking crestfallen as the grizzled hunter repeated what the farmer and his wife had told him.

Kolrim stood next to him looking out into the distance, the proprietor of the Mage’s shop squinting into the distance as if trying to see what horror could have befallen another innocent child.

The long black fur he wore hid his slight frame; he had let his long raven hair hang loose, no longer bothering with the tight bun he usually wore.

“Yet another who was set to train at Dragon’s keep, the Empresses soldiers came to take her the day before she was set to leave, just like the others” he whispered thoughtfully, the suspicion clear in his words

Jorun, the old hunter looked all the worse for wear, now three weeks into the journey, they had traveled to village after village residents telling the same tale, Nero could see his own anger mirrored in the faces of his companions.

“Ten children messenger, what are they doing with them” Jorun asked irritated shooting a suspicious glance at Kolrim as if accusing the mage of stealing the children himself, the mage simply ignoring the hunter, once again.

It had been clear since they had begun this little journey that the old hunter had no love for those with the power, each story told by the grieving parents seemed to reaffirm his suspicion that the mages were up to no good.

Nero shook his head “The Empress is planning something Jorun, there is no doubt the question is what, what could she be doing with all of these children” he asked lowering his eyes, a shiver running through his body at the thought of what could be happening to those young children.

The hunter nodded, but even his agreement that the Empress was up to something didn’t seem to assuage his suspicion of the Order, his steel blue eyes roved over the mage, as if searching for a crack in the man’s veneer, one that would allow him to confirm his thoughts, Kolrim did not seem to notice, his own eyes focused on the tree line, seemingly lost in thought.

“There is some good news, the child was taken only four days past, I have found a trail and I think we might be able to catch them” the hunter said, his tone hopeful.

Nero nodded but kept his thoughts to himself, what would the three of them do, hold up an entire squad of seasoned soldiers and demand answers he wondered, only one of them was actually trained to fight, but maybe he thought, a glimmer of hope by way of a plan began to form in his mind, if they could discover the location of where the children had been taken, the they could rally the support of their orders, bring this to their attention and In doing so gain support and go after them he mused.

Looking at his compatriots, Nero nodded, if they could find the children, and on the off chance an opportunity emerged maybe they could save them, without needing to bring the order or the church into it, despite his initial thought Nero had reservations about both, he had a suspicion that some in his church and a few in Kolrim’s order new about what the Empress was up to and either helping her or turning a blind eye,, he knew they were teetering on the edge, the last thing any of their perspective organizations wanted was to declare war on the other, bringing this to them would be to prove a flagrant violation of the Agreement,, the one treatise that had allowed everyone to live in peace for over a hundred years, Nero, decided to keep these thoughts to himself, nodding a simple agreement to the old hunter.

“Let’s do it Jorun, see if we can track the child” he said, Kolrim finally snapping out of his contemplation. “Can you really track them?” he asked turning towards Jorun who rolled his eyes at the distracted mage’s late entry into the conversation.

Squinting at the mage, again that suspicion evident in his eyes, Jurin simply nodded at him, turning he walked down the hill.

The two men looked after the hunter, the old man mumbling angrily to himself, “What’s his problem?” Kolrim huffed, annoyed, Nero simply shook his head, smiling at his friend “Old wounds my friend, just old wounds, not everyone has had good experiences with mages” he finished.

Clapping the confused mage on his back Nero motioned for him to follow as he went after the old hunter, the two stopping far enough back to give the old man plenty of room to do his work undisturbed.

Jorun paused every so often, studying a plant or a branch before moving forward again, carefully eyeing the ground, every once in a while, he would correct his direction and continue on, the two continuing to follow silently in his wake.

Nero regarded the mage, the two had not been friends and only really banded together at concern for the small girl and fellow villager, but since starting this little quest, Nero had gained a healthy respect for the mage.

He was gentle and cared deeply for people in fact if he had not been given the gift, Nero was sure this man would have made an excellent Messenger.

“Something is bothering you Kolrim, it has been for a few days, what is it?” Nero asked studying the mage.

Kolrim stared out over the land as the rolling hills extended into the distance, the weather looked like snow Nero thought following the other man’s gaze.

After a time, the mage turned towards Nero his expression troubled. “Some of the children who were taken, were known to my order, but not yet to the Monarchy” he simply said, and Nero thought about this, following the line of thought. After a moment his eyes went wide.

“We have suspected as much, but what you’re saying lays the blame at the feet of your order?” he stated, the implication that someone in the Order of the Dragon and the Monarchy were conspiring to take children was enough to make the Messenger reel back.

Nero let his mind wander for a moment down that path, at worst the Order and the Empress were working together, the church would never stand for it, it would shift the balance of power and they would have to respond.

It would mean war he reflected; at best a rogue member of the Order was feeding information to the Empress, which meant that the Order itself could not be trusted with the knowledge that they knew about the disappearances.

The situation was not looking good, one meant war, the other meant their certain death with event the scant knowledge they possessed he reflected, his mood turning sour.

Kolrim thought about it for a moment and Nero could see him putting his thoughts in order, his dark brooding eyes searching for the right phrase.

“I think someone or multiple someone’s might be involved, and it would be someone high up in the order, I don’t think this is an order mandate, I know too many of the guild leaders, they would not go for something like this, but a singular member could do it, but proving it would be another problem, then there is the fact that if the order finds out, they might very well sweep I under the rug fearing people would think It was the order and that possibility could not be entertained” he finished Nero following his line of reasoning, they walked in silence, both men following the mages line of thought, both knowing it would not end well for them either way, Nero focused on the problem at hand, Kolrim brought them back on point, his statement breaking Nero from the thoughts of faraway problems and politics.

“The last two houses saw parent’s dead who protested the taking of the children, that is not something they would do if their actions were above board” Kolrim said, Nero could see the hurt and sorrow in the man’s face and hear it in his words.

This bothers him greatly the Messenger thought still studying Kolrim, “Somehow this is all tied together Nero, nothing we have seen is an isolated incident, there have been disturbing reports as battalions of Vicor’s soldiers move out across the land, taking up position near cities and villages, rumors of coming conscriptions have leaked from the palace, causing young men everywhere anxiety at the thought.

There is even talk that the Empress is set to move out against our neighbors, since the death of the Emperor, advisors and lords have gone missing or been killed in mysterious accidents.

I know not what her goal is, but something is shifting in this land and not for the better” he finished, his words had a ring of the prophetic Nero thought.

Reflecting on this, Nero thought of the reports he had received from the church in the past six months, there had been a lot talk of movement of troops and even the cooperation between the church and monarchy which had been solid for many generations had withered.

The crown no longer advising or informing the church of its intentions, Horsten, the resident advisor and Ambassador during the time of the emperor had been dismissed and sent back to the keep despite the Lord Reagent’s stern protests, Kolrim is right he thought something is happening and its coming to a head, and soon.

The two men walked in contemplative silence watching as the hunter continued studying the ground and moving west.

They spent the next few hours thinking over what they had discussed until Jorun finally stopped, standing at a crossroads he waited impatiently for the two men to catch up to him.

Approaching, Nero caught of the hunters face, fraught with worry as his eyes darted to the different routes leading away from their position.

“What is it, what’s wrong?” he asked almost panicked, this is not a man who is spooked easily he thought, Jorun looked down the worn dirt road, then back at his two companions.

“They went this way, towards the town of Loprik, it’s a small fishing village, there is no reason why they would go there, it is a dead end” The Hunter finished, then it dawned on Nero, “they are going for another child”, and the old hunter nodded in agreement.

“I think so” Jorun began, then hesitated as he gathered his thoughts, “but something else, the troops came back this way” he began, kneeling down as he pointed at the imprints of the soldiers boots, moving to another area of the road, he gently dusted off an area and pointed, Nero squinted, trying to get a better look at what the old man was showing him.

“There is another set of tracks leading back to the village as well, they are, odd…” he said and as he did fear flashed over his face, Kolrim didn’t catch it but Nero did.

“What’s wrong?” he prodded the hunter, who looked down as if embarrassed. “The tracks are strange, Messenger. stories have spread among those of my profession, stories of white demons with glowing eyes, I haven’t put much stock in it. It is said they walk on two or four legs, comfortable moving as man or beast, it is said they serve the Black Queen,” he finished and then pointed to the tracks.

“Are you saying these things serve the Black Queen?” he asked and the old hunter shrugged “That is what I have heard, though I have not seen these things, simply stories from people who I know aren’t prone to fancy” Jurin finished and looked up to see Nero looking off into the distance.

The Messenger had known of the Empress’s nickname for quite some time, everyone had simply thought it commoners being crass, but the more they discovered on this trip, the more Nero thought that the nickname was well deserved.

“Normally I would have simply dismissed them as the tracks of farmers, but look at this,” Jorun began, pointing at the large barefoot prints in the dirt

“They move from two feet, to four and then sprint” he finished, gently running his finger along the contour of the marks on the road.

Kolrim came over to stand next to the print in the road and knelt, looking it over he carefully he reached into the brown leather satchel that hung low on his hip, after a few moments he came out with a vial of something bright blue.

Nero took a step forward trying to get a better look at the contents as the mage upended it over the imprint, as the two men watched the Mage moved his hand over the track whispering words that Nero did not understand.

The reaction, however, was instantaneous as the dust that covered the print began to pulse with a bright light that matched the color of the dust.

The smoke rose in tendrils, the pace of Kolrim’s chanting increasing as the small pillars snaked up towards the sky, they began weaving in and out of each other, Jorun spat to the ground and whispered a curse, walking away from the overt display of magic, Nero let him go, more interested in the smoke coalescing into a form in front of him, it slowly formed as the smoke weaved itself, first a leg, then another, as Nero continued to watch with interest, the smoke turned into a human silhouette. He looked on amazed at the detail, the smoke roiling but maintaining the form of the person.

“What is this?” Nero breathed taking another step forward to get a better look at the smoky specter.

Kolrim smiled with no small amount of pride, “A little spell I have been working on, it takes the echo of energy left behind by creatures of magic, creating a simulacrum from the smoke” he finished looking over the mist born.

Both men took an involuntary step back at the same time as they got a good look at the ‘demon’.

“Aurtus save us” The Messenger whispered, the creature looked human, in the loosest sense of the word, but there was something almost animalistic about him, the way he hunched over as if stalking something or someone, the head was malformed, the skull looking about half a size bigger than it should.

Nero also noticed the creature’s limbs looked too long “Is this right?” he asked circling the still moving smoke. Kolrim stood back, his face a mask of concern and fear “yes, it is Nero, this is what Jorun’s demon looks like,” he whispered.

They stood inspecting it until finally, mercifully the spell expended itself the green smoke dissipating leaving the men staring at nothing.

Turning he noticed his friends face, a look of abject fear warping the normally mild features.

“What’s wrong?” Nero asked concerned, the Mage shook his head.

“When a mage passes through the world, our perception is not like that of mundane’s, the gift manifests itself in different ways, some Mages, like myself, have the ability to see the fabric that connects all living things, like a lake that is imposed over the world, when someone with the gift has passed through an area, it leaves… ripples, the stronger they are magically, the more ripples they leave, it’s not a gift all mages have but it is one that I do, which is why I was assigned as a crystal smith to our village, I have exposure to all the members of the community, I can see when people have power, I am a recruiter in a way, for the order, my ability allowing me to see those with the gift” he stated.

Judging by his friends’ discomfort with the subject, Nero suspected he was intimating to something that was not known outside of the Order.

Kolrim motioned with his hand, waving it over the area in front of the group.

“Whatever made these tracks, had power but it’s… wrong” he said trying to put into words what he saw.

“It’s twisted somehow, I can’t explain it but it’s not like any footprint I have ever seen, Nero, these creatures are not Mages, but they are also not human” he finished trying to put into words something he, himself didn’t quite understand, finally, shaking his head, he looked down the road, his face still showing fear.

Jorun leveled his own gaze at the two, “We should check it out” he stated, the look on his face expecting a challenge from his compatriots but receiving none, Jorun turned back to the road and began walking without another word.

Both of his friends were frightened, whatever was happening fell outside the brigands and thieves that was the usual threats of this world, something was changing in Vicor, something twisted had shown itself and they were now just beginning to see it, to understand.

Kolrim sighed, stepping forward towards the direction of the village, closing his eyes Nero watched as the Mage’s fingers began to dance in the air, as if playing an imaginary piano, the mage once again began whispering in a foreign tongue, the words repetitive and almost rhythmical. As he watched the blue aura of power began gathering in front of him, forming into the shape of a large spectral crow that hung frozen in the air, pulsing with a blue light. In a moment Kolrim flung his fingers forward and the spectral crow took off towards the small village.

Nero stepped up next to his friend “That was amazing” be breathed and then turned gasping as he looked over the mages milky white eyes “Do not be bothered, my eyes are not here, they are with the crow, I see what it sees” he simply said and Nero nodded, after a moment he chided himself realizing the mage couldn’t see him “I see” he followed up, continuing to study the white eyes, a moment later the color returned along with a disturbed look on the mages face. “We have to hurry, there are bodies everywhere” he said and then began walking towards the village, the two other men running to catch up.

They made their way towards the small fishing village, their eyes scanning the tree line constantly, if another child had been taken, they needed to know, even if it was just to report it to their perspective organizations, despite his doubts about the loyalties of some within the Order and the Church, both men had a duty and one they took seriously. But he couldn’t shake the mages words about bodies, what were they walking into he wondered.

The group walked in silence, following the ancient dirt road, everyone keeping an eye out as thoughts of the hunter’s ‘white demon’ still fresh in their minds.

Nero shivered as the Smokey image played back in his mind, Jurin seemed to know quite a bit about the creatures, however Nero himself had nothing from the intelligence delivered to him from the church, did that mean that the Empress now controlled the flow of information or was it as simple as they had not heard anything, either scenario was disturbing he reflected, his mind returned to the rendition of the creature, the smokey but detailed outline showing enough details to carve itself into his nightmares, he had no idea a mage could do that.

Shaking his head Nero admonished himself, he was sure there was a lot of things a mage could do that wasn’t common knowledge to most he reflected, when the agreement was drafted, a few of their abilities had been made public listed in the original document by Zathris himself, over time those gifts had diminished, however that didn’t mean they were gone, nor did it mean, all had been revealed by the order.

Nero wasn’t naive enough to think the Mages had given away all their gifts to the mundane’s, but that fact that Kolrim had thought this creature was important enough to expose one such was testament enough to how much it had bothered the mage.

Both of his traveling companions had been spooked, as was he, the words the old hunter had spoken sounded more like superstition then fact.

Part of him wanted to dismiss it out of hand and yet he had seen the smoke, seen the creature, parts that might have looked human or at least a passing resemblance of one, but it was different enough to cause fear in any that laid eyes upon it.

He was a Messenger of Aurtus, his job was faith, he preached to his flock to believe in that which they could not see, yet he himself had no faith, he had a love of his job and a love for his people, but secretly, Nero had lost his faith many years ago he reflected hanging his head in shame as he did when the doubt came to haunt him.

Nero resolved himself to caution, he might not believe the creatures were demons, but he had seen enough there was more to this world than that which could be explained.

They continued to walk as the sun passed through the sky, eventually settling just above the trees, as the bright white of mid-day turned to the coppery hue of dusk, it was then the trio caught there first sight of water peeking through the ancient oak forest.

The muddy blue a contrast to gnarled brown trunks of the forest, knowing they were getting closer to the village Jorun and Kolrim became more agitated leaving Nero to wonder if maybe they should turn around, go back and follow the main road towards their original destination, tracking the soldiers instead of learning the fate of yet another child, really he thought what could they possibly learn that they didn’t already know he began and stopped himself, realizing the logic was coming from fear.

He didn’t want to know about the child, more importantly about what part that creature might have played in its abduction he thought, but he forced himself forward, not allowing the fear to dictate his actions, as they continued walking the old trade road, the first signs something wasn’t right began to surface as the smell of burning wood was quickly followed by a pyre of black smoke rising in the distance.

“This will not end well” Kolrim whispered, and all Nero could do was nod. Coming over the hill they caught there first sight of the village, or what was left of it.

The group stopping as it the destruction came into full view all, the three men stared at the charred remains of buildings, piles burnt wood all that remained of the once happy little village.

“By Aurtus, what happened” Nero asked to no one as the group sped up their pace, frantically looking for any sign of people. Coming closer they caught the first sight of bodies strewn around the wreckage of the town, from the wounds most looked as if they died running.

Who would do this? Nero thought, stooping to examine the body of a young woman, studying the wound he listened to sound of frantic footsteps while Kolrim and Jurin went from body to body looking desperately for any signs of life, after a few moments he heard them slow, looking up he saw the grim looks on their faces, it was the only answer Nero needed, closing his eyes he quietly whispered a small prayer, mostly from reflex.

Nero stared down at the young woman before him his eyes drawn to the wounds, her body had been clawed, the marks deep through her clothing and skin. “By Aurtus” he whispered kneeling as he examined the jagged slashes masked in blood. “That wasn’t an animal”, came the voice of the old hunter from over Nero’s shoulder, the voice causing him to jump, it was so close it might as well have been his own conscience uttering the words.

Jorun studied the body poking gently at the wounds. “Claw marks, deep ones, but I have never seen anything like this” he said his eyes wide as he looked to the other two. Kolrim also gaining interest in the body had moved over to get a better look, he just stared a look of abject fear on his face as he studied the still warm body.

“What is it?” Nero asked, looking to the mage he could see the small coppery light shining deep within his normally blue eyes. Mage sight, he thought, having heard of this, a mage had the ability to see residual traces of spent magic, he recalled. Nero eyed the man fascinated, having never actually seen anyone do this as Kolrim continued to examine the body of the young girl.

Kolrim shook his head “Something about these wounds, it’s not right” he whispered and then nothing, whatever he was seeing disturbed the mage to the point where his ability to speak escaped him, Nero didn’t press instead moving to the next body.

six bodies later they had almost given up when in the distance they heard a groan. The three running towards the water and the sound, there by the shore covered in sand, was an old man, bloodied and beaten but very much still alive.

Nero made it first to him, gently moving to cradle him in his arms as he put a hand over a wound attempting to staunch the nearly mortal wound over his mid-section. Kolrim was there a heartbeat later, ripping at cloth he had pulled from his pack and quickly dressing the wound, the white cloth staining red the moment it was applied.

Jorun kept his distance, keeping an eye on the tree line, everything about his posture was tense, Nero realizing the grizzled hunter was keeping guard, his fingers lightly caressing the sandalwood grips of the pistols slung low on his hips, every noise causing them to twitch while his compatriots desperately fought to keep this old man alive.

Eyeing the old hunter as his hands worked to save a life, he recognized the body language, this man is scared to death he thought, a moan causing him to divert his attention back to his patient.

“Can you tell us what happened?” Nero asked gently, fussing over the man’s wounds, trying to stop the life-giving blood from leaving his body.

The old man looked up, finally seeing Nero, his eyes lighting on the robes of his office.

“Messenger, please don’t let me die without a blessing” he said panicked, Nero calmed him, “You’re not going to die my son, be calm, your soul is accounted for” he stated, and the old man seemed to relax.

His short white beard was covered in sand held fast by blood from a long set of gashes down his face, they had hence stopped bleeding, but the wounds still looked deep, and Nero worried about infection as he glanced at Kolrim who hung his head and shaking it subtly gave the Messenger a grave stare.

Nero understood, this man wouldn’t live long, he said a silent prayer for his soul. “Please, tell us what happened here” he urged, the old man locking his gaze on the Messenger.

“The soldiers Messenger, they came, they tried to take Kila, but her parents wouldn’t let them, they kill Hurst, her father.

We drove them off, but there were losses” he began and there was both pride and sorrow in his voice as tears fell freely. The pride changed to fear as the old man tensed, his eyes going wide as the memory of the night before continued.

“The soldiers left Messenger, we cheered and celebrated, but as night fell, they came”.

“It’s okay, you are safe” Nero soothed as he held the old man, like a fearful child, he reassured him and soothed him as best he could as tears streamed down his own cheeks. “Messenger, the demons, they came at night they killed everyone, white creatures with glowing eyes, they wailed like the dead and moved with a speed that was not possible. We tried to run and tried to hide, but they found us, tearing through our people with those long sharp claws, I managed to crawl away and hide, the screams, oh the screams” he finished his breath becoming shallow as he reached up with the last of his strength and grasped Nero, “Bless me Messenger” he said again.

Nero took a breath. “May Aurtus take you upon his horse, lead you to the land of man beyond the heavens, may he speak of your deeds and celebrate your accomplishments” he said giving the old man the blessing of death. A small smile began to spread across his face as his chest rattled, expelling his last breath.

Nero sat there, cradling the old man as tears streamed down his face “Go with Aurtus my friend, rest well and celebrate your life” he whispered and gently kissed his head.

Kolrim leaned in gently grabbing Nero by the arm. “We have to go Nero” the messenger looked up at him confused “why, we need to bury them, we can’t leave them like this” he said looking over the bodies strewn around the village. Kolrim continued to pull at his arm.

“We have to go Nero; it is getting dark” he said and emphasized his last words by looking towards the woods.

Nero followed his gaze as the final rays of sunlight settled over the village. As they all stared at the dark underbrush of the trees a blood curdling scream rose from somewhere within the woods. Jorun spat a curse and looked to the other two “We go NOW” he said, and Nero was being pulled up, the body of the old man falling from his lap as Kolrim dragged him to his feet. They ran across the common area of the village.

“Where are we going?” Nero asked panicked, his eyes roving over the woods and the burnt buildings, looking anywhere for shelter or protection and there was none.

The village was too small to warrant a real town center, so there was no keep, no building left standing they could shelter in.

Another scream rose up from in front of them, coming from near the gate as the group came up short stopping in their tracks as something flitted across the opening. Nero squinted seeing a thin human silhouette running on all fours, it’s face turned in their direction he almost ran.

It’s cold blue eyes glowed and the thing emitted a snarl disappearing quickly behind the other side of the village’s wall.

Jorun stood there frantically looking for another way out. More screams rose up around them, echoing over the desolate ruins, more answered, coming from the woods to their left and the village wall to there right.

They were surrounded. “What are those things” Kolrim yelled moving in a circle trying to get a view of them as branches snapped and the sound of claws scraping wood emanated from around them.

“They are playing with us” the old hunter said, dropping into a crouch, bringing his pistols to bear towards the woods, fanning them quickly from sound to sound “We need to move” he said gritting his teeth as another branch snapped close by.

Nero stood there, frozen in fear as the last rays of the sun settled below the trees.

Kolrim grabbed him, pulling him back towards the old man, as the screams continued to roll from all around them.

“What are you doing” he screamed at the mage shaking his hands off of him.

“The water, we need to get to the water” he said grabbing the Messenger yet again and dragging him back, Nero allowed himself to be pulled, “Jorun, let’s go” he yelled as Kolrim pulled him towards the shore.

Kolrim let go, but before Nero could turn to follow his friend he was stopped in his tracks, his eyes going to the ruins of a building as one of the creatures jumped atop a broken support, standing fully erect, its glowing eyes coldly stared at the messenger.

It looked almost human, but also wrong at the same time as if it was a creature trying to mimic a man. He stood staring, not able to move as the creature calmly regarded the small group with those cold, glowing blue eyes.

Then with a casual gesture it pointed its too long arm towards the group, one of its sharp claws extended towards Nero, before he could react a blue bolt shot out from the claw slamming into the dirt in front of him. Nero was thrown back as he heard the frustrated scream of the creature as it missed.

“It’s a mage Kolrim, Memphis’s ass, it’s a mage” he screamed, Kolrim helping him to his feet. “It’s not a mage Nero, its wrong somehow, that’s not mage magic, not like I know it anyway” he said pulling the man towards the shore again.

“Jorun, come on” Nero screamed, the other man still in a crouch with his weapons out.

The old man turned towards the two of them and Nero could see the determination and resignation of his fate in his eyes. “Someone has to hold them off Messenger, go, pray for my soul” he said and then bolted towards the creature on the building.

“No! Jorun, don’t” he called trying to go after the old man, but Kolrim had a death grip on him. “Come on, we have to go “he screamed practically dragging Nero to the shore.

Once they reached the edge of the water Kolrim dragged Nero into a small fishing boat and shoving the small wooden boat off he frantically searched the bottom before coming up with oars.

He began to paddle frantically, Nero watching in horror as the old man reached the building, crouching and brandishing his pistols.

He watched as Jorun fired the gun at the creature, the bolts of blue light deflecting as the creature made a casual motion with its hand, dropping the spent weapon Jorun pulled a long hunting knife from his belt and began to circle the creature.

Three more creatures appeared around the hunter, circling Jorun like a pack of hungry wolves.

Screaming at the old hunter as they circled, once in a while one would step in and take a swipe at him, quickly moving back as the hunter slashed. down with the knife barely missing the creatures each time. “They are playing with him” Nero realized in horror.

Before they could lose sight of the small group Nero watched as the creatures got bored, all four pouncing on the old man at once, descending upon him as claws came down, slashing into his friend.

The last thing Nero heard was the blood curdling screams of the hunter as the beasts tore him apart. Lowering his head, he whispered a blessing for the old hunter.
